title: Truth and Divine Mercy
english: Truth is spoken of in the Savior and in the [psalm where] God sent His mercy and His truth and rescued my soul from the midst of troubles (Ps 117:1). Thus truth and the hope of the nations are one; therefore, having shone upon the human race, it calls all the nations and all the peoples, teaching [them] to give thanks to the Father who strengthens His mercy and makes His truth remain unto the age.

Since God is good and wills the repentance of the sinner rather than his death, you who are responsible for sin, by performing confession through repentance upon him, you will have him forgiving those for whom you confess. For His mercy is found inseparable from Him unto the age, since it is always [so]; in His mercy, not only now but also formerly from the beginning, all those having experience of His goodness confess to Him.

A righteous man having become in affliction does not so much entreat to be outside of it, but how to bravely and cheerfully bear it (Ps 117:5–9). For indeed the one being distressed in the stadium against opponents does not wish the contest to pass by him, lest he become exhausted, but entreats the trainer to cooperate with him, so that, strengthening himself against those advancing toward the opponent, he may win with the hope of victory and the glory of the crown which is given through which the crown is granted.

And it is possible to say different things concerning mortals, 'I shall not fear what man shall do to me' (Ps 117:9), but concerning invisible enemies, 'I also shall see my enemies' (Ps 117:8); for some enemies are even the men who rise up against us, waging war against us and setting themselves against us lethally. And if 'I shall not fear what man shall do to me' is referred to the devil, because 'Man has made this,' it is evident what it is: to sow the weeds (Matt 13:25) and 'But you...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
